subject: Observability egress hardening & SIEM onboarding
messages:

Subject: Observability egress hardening & SIEM onboarding

Thanks Sean / Marissa —

We're starting onboarding for Redwood in our VPC and need to lock down how observability traffic (logs, metrics, traces) leaves our environment to the Splunk HEC endpoint. Two quick constraints from our security team:

- No direct internet egress from workload subnets — all outbound must go through the approved egress clusters/proxies.
- Tokens/keys used for HEC must be short-lived and rotate automatically (we'd like a recommended rotation cadence).
- We need an auditable handoff: which fields are retained at source (PII redaction) and which fields are sent to Splunk.

I've attached the initial network diagram and a short checklist of acceptance items. Can you spell out:
1) recommended topology for forwarding logs/traces from private on-prem agents (sidecar vs centralized forwarder)
2) TLS/mTLS expectations and certificate placement (Redwood side and our egress proxy)
3) sampling / span preservation guidance for tracing hooks so we can correlate request ids to logs

We're on a tight timeline for certification next week — any short-term mitigations (e.g., temporary forwarder in a DMZ) would be helpful.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Security Engineering
Acme Payments

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Logan — thanks for the clear constraints and the diagram, that helps. High level answers below; I'll follow with a one-page topology + checklist we can use for your security review.

1) Topology (recommended):
   - Primary: lightweight sidecar forwarder per infra node that streams JSONL logs and OTLP traces to a local egress aggregator in the VPC (HA pair).
   - Egress aggregator sits in a dedicated subnet with a NAT/egress proxy that has outbound allow-listing to your Splunk HEC endpoint. This avoids direct internet access from app subnets.
   - Fallback: customer-managed DMZ forwarder if policy blocks in-VPC aggregators during certification.

2) TLS / mTLS:
   - Short answer: use mTLS between Redwood forwarders (sidecar -> aggregator -> Redwood forwarder) inside the VPC; TLS (HEC over HTTPS) to Splunk.
   - Identity placement: keep private keys in your KMS/HSM for the aggregator host. We recommend issuing leaf certs per aggregator with an internal CA you control; for mutual auth to Redwood control plane we support cert provisioning via our PKI integration (API token exchange + ephemeral certs).
   - Token rotation: rotate HEC tokens every 24 hours for production; if rotation automation isn't ready, 7-day rotation with auditable issuance logs as mitigation.

3) Tracing hooks & sampling:
   - Preserve trace/span ids in a named field (redwood.trace_id) and include a request_id header on the service layer.
   - Use adaptive sampling: keep 100% of error traces and a configurable percentage (e.g., 5%) of successful traces. Redwood's tracer can attach full KV cache context for sampled spans — helpful for debugging without sending all spans.

Short-term mitigations: stand up a single DMZ forwarder (temporary) and approve its egress IP in Splunk HEC allowlist. We can generate per-forwarder HEC tokens and a rotation script you can run as a cronjob until automated rotation is in place.

I'll attach the topology PDF and a one-page acceptance checklist.

—
Sean Gallagher
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational specifics we use in private deployments that should map directly to your SIEM acceptance criteria:

- Payload format: JSON Lines (one event per line), with explicit top-level fields: timestamp (RFC3339), host, service, level, redwood.trace_id, request_id, and a payload.data object. We avoid sending full user PII fields; instead send hashed identifiers under payload.uid when needed.
- HEC specifics: use Splunk HEC with TLS; tokens scoped to forwarder id and rotated via our API. Set HEC acknowledgment (ack=true) on high-value events to ensure delivery guarantees during onboarding window.
- Rate and batching: we recommend a 200ms batching window and max batch size 5MB for logs. For traces we stream spans over OTLP with 2s flush for buffered exporters. This balances latency vs throughput and keeps small-burst traffic from saturating the egress link.
- Auditability: include an audit header (x-redwood-forwarder: <forwarder-id>) and send a periodic heartbeat event every 60s to the egress aggregator with a signed digest of recent metadata (sha256).

For the acceptance checklist I attached a filled draft (siem-acceptance-checklist.xlsx) that maps your items to the technical controls above and calls out PD steps if we need a DMZ forwarder.

If helpful, we can lock a call tomorrow to walk Splunk PS through the token rotation flow and aggregator cert placement.
